sources.title: Evidence that the Great Pacific Garbage Patch is rapidly accumulating plastic
sources.publisher: Lebreton et al., Scientific Reports; author-hosted PDF
sources.kind: peer-reviewed original field and modelling research

facts.location: PDF p. 1, Abstract; PDF p. 2, sampling description
facts.fact: Lebreton et al. estimate 79,000 tonnes within a 45,000–129,000 interval over about 1.6 million km², using 2015/2016 surveys. These are historical modeled estimates, not a 2026 inventory.

facts.fact: Chong et al.’s 2023 study reports relatively high concentrations of floating life in sampled parts of the patch.
Site selection and modeling choices matter; the study is not a randomized experiment on cleanup harm.

sources.title: Densities of neuston often not elevated within plastic hotspots territory inside the North Pacific Garbage Patch
sources.publisher: Egger et al., Environmental Research: Ecology; Utrecht University repository

facts.location: PDF p. 3, publication date, affiliations and Abstract; PDF p. 9, Discussion
facts.fact: Egger et al., published 11 July 2024, find that neuston is often not elevated in plastic hotspots within the patch; authors discuss sampling limitations and seasonal variability. Several authors are affiliated with The Ocean Cleanup.
